newsitem.title: USA: Drug firm reverses ostereoporosis in lab animals.
newsitem.headline: Drug firm reverses ostereoporosis in lab animals.

text.p: Biotechnology company Amgen Inc said Thursday it was able to reverse the loss of bone mass in laboratory rats with a genetically engineered copy of a human protein it discovered.
The research and discussion of the potential uses of the compound as a treatment for osteoporosis in humans is published in the April 18 issue of the medical journal Cell.

A spokeswoman for Amgen said the company's discovery came out of its genome project, in which it is working to decode the function of human genes. It initially tested the protein by inserting it into female mice, which showed increased bone density after being treated.

In later research, Amgen created a genetically engineered version of the same protein, which it gave to female rats who had had their ovaries removed in order to create a hormonal balance similar to that of post-menopausal women. The research again showed that the compound increased bone volume in the rats.
Amgen is conducting further preclinical research into the protein and said it is unsure when it might begin tests in humans.
Osteoporosis is a potentially cripplin loss of bone mass that strikes post menopausal women.
